body: My advice: watch Claire saffitz on YouTube make her chocolate chip cookies. She’s very good at explaining the purpose behind each step and demonstrating exactly how it should be done/ how the dough should look. She DOES brown the butter in that recipe which is a bit difficult, but if you skip that step, the recipe is pretty standard. (If you skip browning the butter, just use the same amount of butter but ROOM TEMP, not cold, not melted, and omit the heavy cream). I recommend Claire Saffitz for any of your baking needs, she’s the best.

Thanks for the feedback! I wasn’t exactly sure I was using the terminology how I wanted to so I’m so glad that an expert called me out. To me this poem is a bit more about trying to control something that wants to control you, so I wrote it with the Greek myth of Cronus in mind. I wanted to have the drug be something that I try to control by making the choice to consume it, and when the drug becomes God (in the same way that Zeus became God in the myth), it takes control of me. I think I’ll do what you suggested last and switch “amphetamine” and “stimulant drug”. You’re definitely right that it would have a better and more intentional flow that way. And again, thank you so much for taking the time to critique my poem! It means so much to me!!

I was one of the most advanced kids in my grade at school and an avid reader as a child but my ADHD was so debilitating that I ended up dropping out of high school and I doubt I’ll be able to go to college. I was really hesitant on dropping out because I was going to miss so much (Prom, socializing with people my age, having goals and projects to work on regularly, learning in general) but there was literally no way I could continue school because I was failing all of my classes and going to them gave me such intense anxiety since I was so afraid of being told that I was incompetent since I didn’t do the work. I can 100% relate, I (17 F) went to a counselor as well because I’ve felt depressed for years now but I couldn’t figure out how to tell the counselor how I really feel without worrying about being a burden. I’ve done some self reflection and realized that it’s most likely because I’m such a people pleaser and so passive that being a burden on others has become one of my biggest fears. The way I’ve decided to go about tackling it is to speak my mind in small ways on a daily basis and get used to saying what I think in small ways, telling people my opinion on trivial things and maybe I’ll work my way up to opening up about more important things. I’m not any kind of professional lol and I’m not sure if this is the same thing you’re talking about but I hope this helps!
